subject: chemistry
title: Theory vs Reality: Polarisation and Covalent Character
welcome_lead: Compare theoretical and experimental lattice enthalpies.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on lattice enthalpy theory vs experiment.
final_note: You spotted covalent character hiding in ionic compounds.

concepts.def: Partial electron sharing in ionic bond.

walkthroughs.body_html:
If experimental LE > theoretical, compound has more covalent character. NaCl values agree well (mostly ionic).

AgCl experimental is more exothermic than theoretical: Ag+ has high polarising power leading to covalent character.

Small, highly charged cations (Al^3+, Mg^2+) polarise large anions (I-, S^2-) most.

Fajans' rules: covalent character grows with small cation, large anion, high cation charge.

AgI is much more covalent than AgF: I- is large and polarisable. AgI low solubility in water.

Anhydrous AlCl3 has covalent character; sublimes at 178 deg C, forms Al2Cl6 dimer with dative bonds.
